optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Conversational AI Engineer, Support Chat Assistant

professionalSummary.text: Senior AI engineer with 2.5 years of experience building intent classification and answer retrieval models for a SaaS support chat assistant, including end‑to‑end training, evaluation, release preparation, and documentation.
professionalSummary.witness: Trained and evaluated intent classification and answer retrieval models for the support chat assistant in the model development sandbox, using the annotated conversation corpus and a replay set of anonymised past conversations as the held‑out evaluation data.

experienceHighlights.text: Designed and maintained an offline evaluation harness that scores candidate models on intent accuracy, retrieval recall, and replay‑set regressions before release.
experienceHighlights.witness: Built and maintained the offline evaluation harness that scored every candidate model on intent accuracy, retrieval recall and replay‑set regressions before it was proposed for release.

experienceHighlights.text: Prepared release candidates for the assistant platform team, coordinating with the release pipeline and documenting responsibilities, but did not have access to live conversation data.
experienceHighlights.witness: Prepared release candidates for the assistant platform team, which held the release pipeline, the live dashboards and the on‑call rota; my involvement ended at the release review, and I did not have access to the live conversation data.

experienceHighlights.text: Authored model cards and release notes detailing training data cuts, replay‑set results, and known failure modes, ensuring transparency of model limitations.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the model card and the release notes for each candidate model, listing the training data cut, the replay‑set results and the known failure modes on multi‑intent messages.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Evaluation harness report for the last three release candidates and the model card for the intent classifier.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the evaluation harness report for the last three release candidates with sandbox experiment identifiers, and the model card for the intent classifier.

skills.text: Python, PyTorch, scikit‑learn, data engineering, model evaluation harness development, model card authoring, release pipeline coordination.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s experience in training, evaluating, and documenting intent and answer models, as well as coordinating releases with the platform team. They do not establish that the candidate has released models into live traffic, monitored deflection or hand‑off rates, or handled on‑call incidents.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate has strong evidence for training, evaluation, release preparation, and documentation, but lacks evidence of live‑traffic release, monitoring, and incident handling.

role.roleTitle: Conversational AI Engineer, Support Chat Assistant

evidence.text: Prepared release candidates for the assistant platform team, which held the release pipeline, the live dashboards and the on‑call rota; my involvement ended at the release review, and I did not have access to the live conversation data.
evidence.notes: Shows release preparation but no evidence of live deployment or monitoring.

missingEvidence: Evidence that models were actually deployed to live traffic and that deflection/hand‑off rates were monitored.
No record of handling post‑release regressions or mis‑routing spikes; only a note that the platform team carried the pager.

evidence.text: Prepared release candidates for the assistant platform team, which held the release pipeline, the live dashboards and the on‑call rota; my involvement ended at the release review, and I did not have access to the live conversation data.

evidence.text: Built and maintained the offline evaluation harness that scored every candidate model on intent accuracy, retrieval recall and replay‑set regressions before it was proposed for release.
evidence.notes: Shows training and evaluation against held‑out and replay sets.

evidence.text: Wrote the model card and the release notes for each candidate model, listing the training data cut, the replay‑set results and the known failure modes on multi‑intent messages.
evidence.notes: Documents model limitations and hand‑over conditions.

No evidence of handling post‑release regressions or mis‑routing spikes; only note that platform team carried the pager.

interviewSignalRisks.text: Candidate said he had 'shipped the intent models that run the assistant' and that 'my models handle about a million conversations a month'; asked about incidents, he described a replay‑set regression found before a release and said the platform team 'carried the pager'.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify live deployment and incident handling through logs or platform metrics.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide evidence (e.g., release notes, dashboards, or logs) that your intent and answer models were deployed to live customer traffic and that you monitored deflection and hand‑off rates?
Describe a specific incident where a post‑release regression or mis‑routing spike occurred and how you handled it as part of the on‑call rota.

humanReviewChecklist: Confirm that the candidate’s release preparation aligns with the platform team’s pipeline.
Verify that the candidate has no direct access to live conversation data.
Assess the credibility of the recruiter note regarding live traffic and incident handling.
Determine if additional evidence can be obtained to satisfy req_6e1a2c13f2ff and req_00e307158d51.
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The candidate demonstrates strong capabilities in model training, evaluation, release preparation, and documentation, satisfying several key requirements. However, critical gaps remain regarding live‑traffic deployment, monitoring, and incident response. Human review should focus on obtaining concrete evidence for these gaps before proceeding with an offer.
limitations: Evidence is limited to the provided resume, work samples, and recruiter notes; no external verification of live deployment or incident logs is available.
